entry.title: [推荐] Rethinking (De)growth: the politics of compost
entry.content:
Contemporary Political Theory · Vol. 25 No. 1 · 推荐 (5.0)

Jessica Croteau

Moving beyond economic analyses of degrowth, growth and consumption are reframed through decomposition as a vital process through which life, value, and politics are continually re-composed. Against dominant imaginaries that cast decay as waste or ruination, this article turns to composting and carrion ecologies to articulate decomposition as a generative undoing and a mode of transformation that binds waste to worth. Drawing on multispecies examples from vultures in India to the Baltimore Compost Collective, the article situates decomposition as both material process and political metaphor to enact a revaluation of growth, decay, and consumption that unsettles capitalist logics of extraction and accumulation. entry.title: [推荐] The subject of intelligence: AI as existential risk and the government of the human and the future
entry.content:
Contemporary Political Theory · Vol. 25 No. 1 · 推荐 (5.0)

Caio Simoneti

This article analyses discourses on artificial intelligence (AI) in the field of existential risk studies. AI appears as a key theme in existential risk circles, not only as a source of risk, but also as a resource for risk prevention and as the enabler of a glorious future for humanity. However, what is it about AI that brings together utopian and dystopian imaginaries? Why is a discourse on AI so tied to questions regarding the human, and what forms of humanity does it produce? What forms of governing does it enable? This article argues that the concept of ‘intelligence’ is fundamental regarding both how AI is construed as an existential risk, as well as how humanity is conceptualised as that which needs to be protected. entry.title: [推荐] Is religion a problem for intersectional theory? Muslim women, feminism, and varieties of patriarchy
entry.content:
Contemporary Political Theory · Vol. 25 No. 1 · 推荐 (3.0)

Karolin I. M. Tuncel、Tobias Müller

Intersectional theory has been criticised for neglecting religion and for being unable to account for religion’s social complexities. This contribution interrogates this critique by disaggregating different relationships of Muslim women to secular and religious varieties of patriarchy. We argue that what demarcates the challenges of intersectional analysis are the political contestations not around religion, but around women’s pro-patriarchal agency. We do so by discussing intersectional theory’s analytical usefulness and limitations in conceptualising the experiences of Muslim women. Political Theory · Vol. 54 No. 5 699-723 · 必读 (7.0)

Rita Koganzon

Political theorists have long focused their understanding of democratic education on the institution of the school, particularly the public school, to the exclusion of broader visions of education beyond schooling. But as criticisms of schooling from outside the academy mount, it becomes imperative to examine the origins of American educational thought to determine whether opposition to schooling has an older historical source. This essay locates the roots of school skepticism in an alternative American educational tradition beginning with Benjamin Franklin that drew on Locke’s pedagogical arguments to devalue institutional schooling in favor of self-education. entry.title: [推荐] The Utilitarian Classical Liberalism of Ludwig von Mises and Its Libertarian Misreception
entry.content:
Political Theory · Vol. 54 No. 5 749-772 · 推荐 (3.0)

Jonathan Cole

This article examines Ludwig von Mises’s utilitarianism in the context of his liberal social theory. It contends that he sought to reorient classical liberalism away from natural law theory and refound it in utilitarianism. This significant shift distinguishes and differentiates Misesian liberalism from the classical liberal tradition with which Mises consciously identified it, as well as later Rothbardian libertarianism, which, while identifying with the Misesian tradition, reverted to a natural law philosophy that produced irreconcilable differences with Misesian liberalism over the legitimacy of the state.

entry.content:
Political Theory · Vol. 54 No. 5 724-748 · 推荐 (3.0)

Nicholas A. Anderson

The fact that Toward Perpetual Peace is presented as a satirical peace treaty is a detail that has been largely overlooked in the literature. This article argues that when one reads Toward Perpetual Peace with its formal presentation in mind, what emerges is a work of philosophical literature that acts politically through its rhetorical form. The article shows how Kant—through what is here called his rhetoric of hope—offers a political education to two kinds of readers: the many, who are susceptible to a “despotic” moralism, and the elite, who embrace the principles of a selfish despotism. Political Theory · Vol. 54 No. 5 653-676 · 推荐 (3.0)

Clare Woodford、Michelle Bentley

This article offers a feminist reworking of Adriana Cavarero’s conceptualization of horrorism as a form of extreme violence that targets and dehumanizes its victims through dismemberment and an ontological assault on human uniqueness. The binary risks reproducing the very logics of exclusion and moral absolutism it seeks to disrupt. Constellations · 预印(online-first) · 必读 (10.7)

E. Lawrence Bradford

In the 1920s and 1930s, Walter Benjamin and Theodor W. Adorno both sought to develop a notion of Darstellung —of philosophical presentation or representation—that could provide an alternative to the classically idealist tendency to subsume objects under abstract concepts. Benjamin's influence on Adorno is therefore often narrativized through the latter's early work, in which Adorno appears as Benjamin's “disciple” in the 1930s before later developing an independent philosophical voice. I seek to complicate this narrative through an investigation of the term “constellation,” which appears prominently in Benjamin's work before being repurposed by Adorno. This article interprets the geological sequestration of carbon dioxide as an opportunity to re-imagine the appropriability of nature and its resources. While the extraction of hydrocarbons was historically supported by radical innovations in the definition of legitimate ownership – most notably the relentlessly expansive interpretation of the ‘rule of capture’ in the United States – the need to inject billions of metric tonnes of CO₂ into the lithosphere to achieve any measure of climate stabilization has not generated any meaningful change in juridical reasoning. Legal and economic constructions of geologically sequestered carbon are for the most part parasitic on the measures of value and the modes of appropriation that legitimize fossil fuel mining. entry.title: [推荐] Authoritarianism's Annihilation Anxieties
entry.content:
Constellations · 预印(online-first) · 推荐 (3.0)

Noëlle McAfee

Using a psychoanalytic lens attuned to preoedipal phenomena, this article argues that neoliberal precarity produces and exacerbates conditions that draw people to fascism. This article shows how neoliberalism produces annihilation anxieties and conditions on which fascism feeds. With mounting anxieties and scant collective means for dealing with them, people easily succumb to fascism's promise of a life raft and safe harbor in precarious times. At bottom, the essence of fascism is its logic for appeasing unconscious demands for ways to ward off debilitating, politically produced anxieties. This logic leads to three overarching fascist delusions: bending reality; a mythic past; and eliminationism. This analysis provides a way to see fascism's deep structure as a palliative that allows a world out of joint continue to be so.

Perspectives on Politics · 1-19 · 预印(online-first) · 推荐 (3.35)

Nicolás de la Cerda、Jacob R. Gunderson

Positional blurring is a common and effective party strategy. It enables parties to downplay some issues while highlighting and clarifying their profile on others. However, we know little about how parties use this strategy outside European party systems, in which (right-wing) populist parties are particularly noteworthy for their blurred economic positions and clear cultural positions. Is that strategy inherent to populism or a reflection of context-specific incentives? This article uses data from Europe and Latin America to argue that populists tailor their strategies to the dimensionality of their party system and populism’s host ideology. entry.title: [推荐] Thomas Paine’s Greatest Revolution: Nationality, Citizenship, and Civic Identity in America
entry.content:
The Review of Politics · 1-23 · 预印(online-first) · 推荐 (3.0)

Richard Boyd

Thomas Paine is widely known for galvanizing public opinion in favor of the cause of American independence; his trenchant critique of Edmund Burke and spirited affirmation of the “rights of man”; and his contribution to the development of republicanism during constitutional debates in France. Yet there has been less scholarly attention to what is arguably Paine’s greatest revolution: namely, his vision of the United States as a “civic nation” whose membership is determined by consent to shared republican principles. A closer examination of Paine’s life and political writings reveals the strengths as well as the weaknesses of this civic ideal.

entry.content:
Constellations · 预印(online-first) · 必读 (8.0)

Ruiqi Yin

This article examines contemporary digital governance through a dialogue between Shoshana Zuboff's theory of surveillance capitalism and Michel Foucault's analysis of power and governmentality. Although Zuboff offers a compelling account of the economic logics underlying digital domination, her framework tends to locate resistance primarily in external regulation and legal reform. This article argues that such an approach overlooks the subjectifying effects through which digital governance shapes compliant and predictable subjects. Drawing on Foucault, it reconceptualizes surveillance capitalism as an intensification of existing governmental rationalities and advances the notion of counter‐conduct to analyze how subjects negotiate and resist digital power from within.

Philosophy & Social Criticism · 预印(online-first) · 推荐 (5.7)

A. Sophie Lauwers

Recent philosophers of secularization have given religion a more central place in their thinking about secular modernity and liberal democracy. This article argues that such theories have overlooked an important dimension of the contemporary social and political landscape, namely how the framework of separating ‘religious’ and ‘secular’ spheres can paradoxically affirm the hegemonic position of Christianity and marginalize non-Christian minorities. Drawing on the work of Gil Anidjar, the article instead develops a critical narrative of secularization which points to continuations of Christian hegemony in the ‘secular’ realm, despite and through the religion-secular binary. This article examines power and resistance in Margaret Atwood’s MaddAddam trilogy through the lens of Foucauldian biopolitics. Combining close textual analysis with political theory and literary studies, it argues that Atwood’s speculative fiction offers a powerful critique of contemporary capitalism by showing how life, bodies, and conduct become sites of government within neoliberal market logics. entry.title: [推荐] When home isn’t home anymore: Towards a political theory of displacement without movement
entry.content:
European Journal of Political Theory · 预印(online-first) · 推荐 (3.0)

James Souter

Normative political theorists typically view displacement as a phenomenon that entails forced movement. In this article, I challenge this orthodoxy by arguing that displacement is fundamentally a loss of one's place and/or home that may occur either with or without such movement. First, the notion allows us to identify a common condition that unites the experiences of those who lose their place and/or home through forced movement and those who lose it in their habitual locations. This paper examines the philosophical foundations of Land's right-wing trajectory and asks how the digital is integrated into his political economy and anti-humanist worldview. entry.content:

Tal Tzur

Critics of neoliberalism increasingly examine its corrosive effects on democracy. Scholars often turn to Friedrich Hayek's political theory, arguing that it produces citizens who passively conform to spontaneous social orders. Yet insufficient attention has been paid to the normative conception of the human individual underlying his neoliberalism. This article demonstrates that Hayek's theory actively rejects individuality, understood as the cultivation and expression of one's distinct personal character. Individuality requires an experimental approach toward social action and critical reflection on whether social rules express one's character, yet such attitudes are systematically stifled in Hayek's account because they threaten the unequivocal obedience his spontaneous orders demand. entry.title: [必读] Adorno and the Kantian Sources of Ideology Critique
entry.content:
Constellations · 预印(online-first) · 必读 (11.35)

Antoine Athanassiadis

Social theorists in the Marxian tradition often interpret philosophical problems as reflections of social problems. This approach is central to Adorno's interpretation of Kant's epistemology. Adorno claims that the Critique of Pure Reason develops a concept of subjectivity that mirrors the “functionalization” of experience in capitalist societies. He retains that concept contradictory just as the social functionalism it ideologically reflects. In this paper I argue that Kant's concept of subjectivity is not contradictory and that Adorno must rely on it to articulate his critique of functionalism. Recognizing this Kantian debt implies not just acknowledging the Kantian sources of Adorno's model of ideology critique, but also revising central aspects of his social theory.

entry.title: [推荐] The Associationist 1848 and the Promise of Socialism
entry.content:
Modern Intellectual History · 1-26 · 预印(online-first) · 推荐 (3.5)

John Mac Kilgore

For the American Fourierist movement known as Associationism, the European revolutions of 1848 represented the opening scene of a new world-historical struggle: “the Emancipation of Labor.” The momentous example of the French Revolution in particular pushed this group of cooperative labor reformers, often dismissed as “utopians,” to embrace the politics and persuasiveness of working-class agitation as a tactical means to reorganize the system of industry. I argue that the Associationists—sidelined, when not forgotten, in the existing scholarship of “the American 1848”—should be appreciated for placing socialism on the agenda as the promise of a future workers’ democracy in the United States. Not only that, but they came to view the US labor movement itself as a participant in the social and political transformations of the 1848 revolutions. This is the Associationist 1848.
